title: QBR CostGuard - Usage & Billing Worksheet
content:
Purpose: quick, conversation-friendly worksheet to drive the usage + billing section of a QBR. Focus: token spend behavior, rate-limit exposure, budget guardrails, and recommended alert/playbook language for account teams.

Audience: CSM + customer finance/ops + solutions engineer. Use during pre-QBR prep, share as appendix at QBR.

HOW TO USE:
- Fill in the top-level numbers (last 30 / 90 / 365 days).
- Highlight any anomalies or 7-day spikes (call them out in the Notes column).
- Pick 1-3 recommended mitigations before next QBR and assign owners.

KEY SECTIONS (suggested order):
1) Quick snapshot (1 line summary)
- Current monthly burn run-rate (excl credits): _________ USD / month
- Avg tokens/day (30d): _______ tokens
- 95p token QPS (30d): _______ qps
- Billing tier / committed capacity: _________

2) Top-5 spend drivers (last 30 days)- Feature / route / integration: 
  - Example: chat_api/v1/generate - 42% of tokens - main web app
  - Example: embeddings/encode - 18% - nightly batch jobs
  - Notes: (are any of these experimental, can be throttled?)

3) Signal checks (automated checks to run pre-QBR) - checklist
- [ ] Total tokens vs forecast: current run-rate > forecast by X%? (calc below)
- [ ] Burst windows: presence of N>1s spikes > baseline by 5x in last 14 days
- [ ] Rate-limit events: number of 429s in last 7 days > 0
- [ ] Failed retries attributable to downstream timeouts (500/502)
- [ ] Budget alerts triggered in last 90 days: count and what action took place

4) Suggested alert thresholds (templates)
- Budget runway: daily spend > 120% of daily forecast for 3 consecutive days -> "Finance: investigate"
- Immediate guardrail: any single job with >5M tokens in an hour -> "Ops: pause job & investigate"
- Rate-limit early-warning: 429s > 0.5% of requests in 1h -> "SRE/CSM: inspect client throttling"
- Cost-regression monitor: model change that increases median tokens per request by >15% after deploy -> "ModelOps + CSM: rollback or opt-in"

Suggested Slack alert format (short):
`[CS-ALERT] account=ACME corp | metric=hourly_tokens | window=1h | value=6.2M | thresh=5M | action=review`

5) Playbook snippets (short runbooks for on-call or CSM)
A. If daily burn > forecast by >20% for 3 days:
  - CSM: send FYI to customer finance, attach token breakdown + top 3 routes.
  - SE: propose immediate quick wins: prefix caching, early stop, reduce max tokens.
  - Ops: schedule throttling window if unresponsive to outreach.

B. If rate-limit 429s spike > 1% in 1h:
  - SE: check client retry strategy + backoff (reduce burst concurrency).
  - CSM: notify customer of degraded experience and suggested mitigation (stagger batch jobs).
  - SRE: consider temporary capacity bump or fallback to cheaper model variant.

C. If single job consumes sudden large tokens (>10M in 1h):
  - Immediately identify job owner (job_id, user_id) -> put job on hold.
  - Ask for code snippet + intended loop shape (is there runaway loop?).
  - Propose quota limit on that API key pending fix.

6) Quick SQL snippets to populate worksheet (example queries)
- 30d total tokens by route (Postgres-like):
  SELECT route, sum(tokens) as tokens_30d
  FROM billing.events
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '30 days'
  GROUP BY route
  ORDER BY tokens_30d desc

- Hourly token spikes (last 7d):
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour, sum(tokens) as tokens_hour
  FROM billing.events
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '7 days'
  GROUP BY hour
  ORDER BY tokens_hour desc

- 429 count by hour (last 14d):
  SELECT date_trunc('hour', ts) as hour, sum(case when status_code = 429 then 1 else 0 end) as c429, count(*) as total
  FROM proxy.requests
  WHERE ts >= now() - interval '14 days'
  GROUP BY hour
  HAVING sum(case when status_code = 429 then 1 else 0 end) > 0

7) QBR talking points (3 bullets, put on slide)
- Usage trend: "Stable/moderate/growing" — call out cause (feature launch, experiments, migrations).
- Risk: any short-term runway gaps or rate-limit exposures and proposed mitigations.
- Opportunity: optimization or quantization recommendations that reduce unit CPI without hurting quality.

8) Customer-facing template language (short)
- Opening: "Thanks — we wanted to share a quick usage snapshot and a few suggested guardrails to keep your apps predictable as you scale."
- If overrun: "We observed sustained run-rate above your forecast. We recommend (1) add a soft quota, (2) implement prefix caching for the top route, and (3) schedule a short runbook call to align on fixes."
- If rate-limited: "We saw transient throttling on X route. Quick mitigation: increase client backoff + limit burst concurrency. Longer-term: we can discuss reserved capacity for that workload."

9) Ownership, action tracker (simple table for the doc)
- Action: tighten prefix cache TTL on chat route | Owner: SE (Marisol) | Due: 1 week | Status: open
- Action: create budget alert with 3-day window | Owner: CSM (Aisha) | Due: 3 days | Status: open
- Action: investigate 429 spike on 2026-02-24 | Owner: SRE (Ethan) | Due: 48h | Status: in_progress

10) Open questions / items to validate with customer
- Was there a code change or new batch job around the spike timestamps?
- Are there internal quotas you want us to enforce (hard vs soft)?
- Will finance accept daily email digests or prefer weekly CSV exports?

Notes to self (raw):
- Bring raw event slices to prep call (last 14 days: top 10 routes by tokens, top 5 users by tokens).
- Check whether embedding jobs are deduped; often they re-run too frequently.
- Confirm if customer is on dedicated capacity — if yes, propose a committed capacity review.

Appendix / Data attachments needed before QBR:
- CSV: tokens_by_route_30d.csv
- CSV: hourly_tokens_7d.csv
- Screenshot: 95p_latency_by_route.png

Draft timeline for QBR section:
- T-minus 5 days: run queries and populate sheet
- T-minus 3 days: internal review + initial outreach if high-risk
- T-minus 1 day: finalize slide and send pre-read to customer finance

End of worksheet.
